title: Who benefits, and are they connected?
question: For the organizations and firms named in files an official sponsored, what recorded links run back to that official?
finding: Sponsored contracts, grant agreements, leases and loans that passed name 461 outside organizations in 813 official-and-beneficiary pairs. In 52 pairs (6.4%) the beneficiary, its staff or a committee it funded appears in the sponsor’s own money records, and in 20 more the only link is a registered lobbyist’s reported contact. The largest money link is Pacific Gas and Electric with Mark Farrell ($27,400; 1 sponsored file naming $10.0 million).
how: Beneficiaries are the counterparties this project’s Board-file table reads from the titles of passed contracts, grant agreements, leases and loans; public bodies are left out. Each is looked up, by exact name after removing punctuation and company suffixes, in the sponsoring official’s records: contributions to the official’s candidate committees by the organization itself or by donors who wrote it as their employer; contributions to a ballot committee carrying the official’s name or to a committee others formed to support the official; payments made or received at the official’s request; gifts and travel the official reported; and lobbyists’ reported contacts with the official on the organization’s behalf. Officers and directors are those the contractor listed on its contract-approval notice (Form 126f4): they are named only when their contribution also names the organization as employer. “Link predates the file” compares the earliest money link with the first sponsored file. “Final vote” is the last Board passage roll call of each file, from the Board’s roll calls on money files (2015 to 2026); members printed “No” are named. “Sponsor on the committee” says whether the vote grid of the committee that sent the file to the Board lists the sponsor.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt. Donors give to officials who already agree with them; an organization’s staff live and vote in the city; the Mayor is the sponsor of more money files than any supervisor, whoever the contractor is; and lobbying is registered. A link here is any link at any date, not a payment for the file. Exact-name matching misses variants (so links are undercounted) and a large employer’s staff giving says little about the employer. Individual donors are counted, never named. Most money files pass without a no vote, so a unanimous final vote says nothing about the sponsor or any other member. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
